text: Traversing a two-dimensional array along its rows is faster than along its columns, because each row occupies contiguous memory and the processor fetches whole ___ lines.
explanation: The difference is measured at about threefold in Chapter 32, for identical operation counts — which is the clearest demonstration in the book that big-O cannot see everything. Both traversals are O(n^2); one keeps the prefetcher right and the other misses on nearly every access. Ulrich Drepper's memory paper, recommended three times in the book, is the full account.
